text:
maya: quick sync — we need concrete threshold definitions/signals for Q3 runtime OKRs. goal is to finalize by EOD Wed so product can lock priorities. sketch below, please call out blockers or alternate bounds.

alex: got it — post the sketch pls

maya: here's the proposal (very intentionally concrete):
```
- Latency (generation): p95 <= 120ms for 512 tokens (hosted p50 target 60ms)
- Throughput: baseline 800 req/sec per GPU @ batch=8 (sustained at 70% peak util)
- KV cache: effective hit rate >= 35% on prefix-heavy workloads (measured server-side)
- Quantization rollout: int8/qat must not degrade eval metric (BLEU/ROUGE) by > 1.5% and client-obs hallucation rate delta <= 0.2%
- Canary gating: no single canary window with error_rate > 0.5% and 99.9th latency <= baseline + 50ms
- Cost signal: per-token cost delta <= +5% vs baseline for hosted config
```

raj: measurement Q — are we using client-observed tail or server-side instrumentation for the p95/p99 gates? we should be explicit.

maya: good call. baseline is server-side request profiling (latency_server_ms) but we will also surface client_obs_latency as a secondary signal for user-facing regressions. canary fails if either shows >5% regression for p95.

taylor: how are we defining "prefix-heavy" for KV hit target? need a deterministic query set.

sam: propose we reuse the customer-ask corpus from the ops bench (50k traces) — define prefix-heavy as >= 3 token overlap in first 32 tokens. that corpus gives a realistic hit distribution.

alex: procedural: launch gating for each model variant requires:
- 3 successful canary windows (6h each) with green metrics
- perf regression < 1% request success and token-cost within +/-5%
- automated smoke tests + 1 manual spot-check from SRE

maya: adding canary config example to standardize:
```
canary_policy:
  duration: 6h
  rollout_steps: [10, 25, 50] # percent traffic
  metrics:
    latency_p95: allowed_delta: +5%
    error_rate: allowed_delta: +0.5%
    kv_hit: allowed_delta: -3%
    cost_per_token: allowed_delta: +5%
```

raj: for quantization we'll need a deterministic eval harness (hooks to compare tokens and scoring). i'll own that. will need a baseline artifact and a quantized artifact run across the 10k eval prompts.

sam: pushing on prioritization — several enterprise customers asked for better KV consistency and TTL tuning. i recommend we prioritize KV hit improvement work in Q3 over broad int8 rollout. that also gives us better short-term latency & cost wins.

taylor: agree; KV fixes are lower risk and unblock many dedicated deployments.

alex: can we put a hard P1/P2 split in the OKR doc? P1 = KV hit improvements + canary infra + telemetry; P2 = quantization broad rollout + kernel reordering experiments.

maya: +1. i'll annotate the OKR doc that way unless anyone objects.

ops-bot: perf test scheduled by sam for 2026-07-12 09:00 UTC — job id perf-20260712-001 — results will be posted to /infra/perf/results/perf-20260712-001

perf-bot: canary run template created: https://redwood.internal/perf/canary-template-v2 (contains metrics/alerts).

alex: quick ask — can we have dashboards with the canonical signals: latency_server_ms_p50/p95/p99, client_obs_p95, kv_hit_ratio, error_rate, cost_per_token? taylor can you own dashboard?

taylor: i'll spin up an initial dashboard + alert rules today and link in the OKR doc.

maya: ownership summary (will add to OKR doc):
- alex: canary config + launch checklist
- raj: eval harness + regression suite for quant
- taylor: telemetry dashboards + alerts
- sam: KV tuning, bench corpora, and perf runs

maya: thanks — i'll update the OKR sheet and present this on Thurs product sync. if no objections by EOD Wed, this becomes Q3 runtime-performance plan. :thumbsup:

alex: :thumbsup:

raj: no objections

sam: all good

perf-bot: test results will be auto-attached to the OKR card after runs complete.
